             Rules of Conduct for Planning Commission Meetings
PROCEDURE FOR PUBLIC COMMENT

1.   Any person or entity may appear in person or be represented by an authorized agent at any meeting of the
     Commission.

2.   Unless altered by the Chair, the order of the procedure on an application shall be:

     a. The supporting agency staff will introduce the application, including staff’s recommendations and a
        summary of pertinent written comments and reports concerning the application

     b. The applicant will be allowed up to 15 minutes to make their presentation.

     c. The Community Council representative can present their comments as applicable.

     d. Where applicable, persons in favor of, or not opposed to, the application will be invited to speak.

     e. Where applicable, persons opposing the application, in whole or in part will be invited to speak.

     f. Where applicable, the applicant will be allowed 5 minutes to provide concluding statements.

     g. Surrebuttals may be allowed at the discretion of the Chair.

CONDUCT FOR APPLICANTS AND THE PUBLIC

1.   Speakers will be called to the podium by the Chair.

2.   Each speaker, before talking, shall give his or her name and address.

3.   All comments should be directed to the Commissioners, not to the staff or to members of the audience.

4.   For items where there are several people wishing to speak, the Chair may impose a time limit, usually 3
     minutes per person, or 5 minutes for a group spokesperson. If a time limit is imposed on any member or
     spokesperson of the public, then the same time limit is imposed on other members or spokespersons of the
     public, respectively.

5.   Unless otherwise allowed by the Chair, no questions shall be asked by the speaker or Commission Members.

6.   Only one speaker is permitted before the Commission at a time.

7.   The discussion must be confined to essential points stated in the application bearing on the desirability or
     undesirability of the application.

8.   The Chair may cease any presentation or information that has already been presented and acknowledge that it
     has been noted in the public record.

9.   No personal attacks shall be indulged in by either side, and such action shall be sufficient cause for stopping the
     speaker from proceeding.

10. No applause or public outbursts shall be permitted.

11. The Chair or supporting agency staff may request police support to remove offending individuals who refuse to
    abide by these rules.

12. After the public comment portion of a meeting or hearing has concluded, the discussion will be limited to the
    Planning Commission and Staff.

                                              File # SUB2024-001074


                          ROADWAY EXCEPTION FOR CORDERO DRIVE
                             SUMMARY AND RECOMMENDATION
Public Body: Magna City Planning Commission
Meeting Date: November 14, 2024
Acreage: 78.48 Acres
Current Zone: P-C (Planned Community) Zone
Property Address: 8230 West 4100 South
Request: Exception to Roadway Standards for Road Grading for proposed Cordero Drive.
Planner: Jeff Miller
Planning Staff Recommendation: Approval
Applicant Name: Ross Dinsdale (Ivory Homes)


                                         PROJECT DESCRIPTION
                                                           Ross Dinsdale (Ivory Homes) is requesting an exception
                                                           to Roadway Standards for the proposed roadway
                                                           grading along Cordero Drive. The proposed grading
                                                           along Cordero Drive does not currently comply with
                                                           Section 14-12-090 (c) of the Magna City Ordinance,
                                                           which states, “All approach legs of intersections shall
                                                           provide vertical crest grades not to exceed two percent
                                                           for a distance of at least fifty feet from the right-of-way
                                                           line of intersecting streets.”

                                                           The overall concept for the Mahogany Ridge
                                                           development was approved by the Magna City Council
                                                           in late 2023 and included an alignment of Cordero Drive
at 8400 West with the Cordero Drive located to the west in the Gateway to Little Valley Planned Community. We
have been working with Ivory Homes, Magna City & the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) to facilitate a
future signalized intersection at Cordero Drive & 8400 West. This signalized intersection will improve the safety of
traffic near the new Cyprus High School opening fall 2025.
Request: Exception to Roadway Standards for Proposed Grading along Cordero Drive.



To help expedite the construction and signalization of Cordero Drive & 8400 West, the Magna City Council approved
an expedited review and approval process for the Mahogany Ridge (Phase 2A) Subdivision Plat granting preliminary
plat approval as part of the development agreement approval.

In order to maintain the existing street layout for the Mahogany Ridge Planned Community, an exception to the
roadway standards for grading along Cordero Drive is needed. If strict adherence to the required grading was
followed, it would require smooth sections of the road where intersections are, and then steeper grading before
and after the intersections.

*See recommendation letter from Engineering for the proposed exception.


                          SITE & VICINITY DESCRIPTION (see attached map)
The Mahogany Ridge Planned Community is located between 4100 South & approximately 3900 South, and
between 8400 West & 8000 South. Phase 1 is located in the northeast corner of the development. To the
immediately north of Phase 1 are similarly sized residential lots in the R-1-5 (Residential, 5,000 SF Minimum) Zone.
There are industrial parcels located in the M-1 & M-2 (Manufacturing) Zones to the north and east of the property.
The Gateway to Little Valley Planned Community is located immediately to the west across 8400 West in the P-C
(Planned Community) Zone.


                         ISSUES OF CONCERN/PROPOSED MITIGATION
The letter of recommendation from Engineering identifies a concern with the close proximity of two streets located
off of Cordero Drive near 4100 West. As a condition of approval, Engineering is requesting that these two streets
be dead ended at Cordero Drive. Ivory Homes is aware of this issue and has agreed to dead end these two streets.
This change will enable the street grading along Cordero Drive to come closer to compliance with the roadway
standards.


                                              STAFF ANALYSIS
Planning Staff is supportive of the proposed exception request, with the conditions of approval as requested by
Engineering with their favorable letter of recommendation.

                                     NEIGHBORHOOD RESPONSE
Planning Staff has not received any comments from the surrounding neighbors or general public as of the
completion of this staff report. Any comments that are received will be forwarded to the planning commission for
review and will be summarized on November 14, 2024.

                                 PLANNING COMMISSION MOTION
The Planning Commission has three options with respect to this application for the requested Exception
Request:
Option 1:      Approve the Roadway Exception as proposed with the conditions as proposed; or
Option 2:      Approve the Roadway Exception with the conditions as amended.
Option 3:      Deny the proposed Roadway Exception.


Exception to Roadway Standards                                                                           Page 2 of 3
Request: Exception to Roadway Standards for Proposed Grading along Cordero Drive.




                              CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Planning Staff recommends that the Magna City Planning Commission grants approval to the proposed exception
to roadway standards for grading along Cordero Drive for the Mahogany Ridge Planned Community, subject to the
following conditions of approval (as requested by Engineering in their favorable letter of recommendation):


    1.   The interesections at Cordero Drive and Madison Peak Way and the private alley across Corder Drive
         opposite of Madison Peak Way be eliminated. These would need to be made into dead end roads, without
         access onto or off of Cordero Drive (with the exception of provisions for temporary emergency vehicle
         access if determined to be needed).


    2.   The applicant meets all other applicable roadway standards and is able to demonstrate, to the satisfaction
         of the Municipal Engineer, that the vertical crest grades within 50 feet of intersection streets have been
         reduced as much as is feasible, short of modifying the overall subdivision layout.

    D.   Favorable Letter of Recommendation from Engineering.

                             Application:    001147 – Ivory, Mahogany Ridge Phase 2A

Kade D. Moncur, P.E., CFM
Director, Public Works
Engineering Division
                             There are several locations along the proposed Eaglehead Way (Cordero Drive)
PUBLIC WORKS                 which do not comply with Section 14.12.090(C) of the Magna City ordinance
ENGINEERING DIVISION         which states:
Government Center            “All approach legs of intersections shall provide vertical crest grades not to exceed
2001 South State Street      two percent for a distance of at least fifty feet from the right-of-way line of
Suite N3-120
Salt Lake City, Utah 84190   intersecting streets”.
T 385-468-6600
F 385-468-6603               It is the recommendation of Salt Lake County Public Works Engineering that an
                             exception be granted for Eaglehead Way (Cordero Drive) needing to comply with
                             this ordinance requirement (Section 14.12.090[C]) only if the following conditions
                             are met:
                                  1. The intersections at Cordero Drive and Madison Peak Way and the private
                                      alley across Cordero Drive opposite of Madison Peak Way be eliminated.
                                      These would need to be made into dead end roads, without access onto or
                                      off of Cordero Drive (with the exception of provisions for temporary
                                      emergency vehicle access if determined to be needed).
                                  2. The applicant meets all other applicable roadway standards and is able to
                                      demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the Municipal Engineer, that the vertical
                                      crest grades within 50 feet of intersection streets have been reduced as
                                      much as is feasible, short of modifying the overall subdivision layout.

                             The applicant claims that in order to completely meet the ordinance requirement
                             the overall subdivision layout would need to be modified. We acknowledge that
                             this may be the case and will not press for that, but the applicant has not sufficiently
                             demonstrated that they have done everything feasible to reduce the grades to get
                             closer to meeting this ordinance requirement without modifying the overall
                             subdivision layout. We believe that the applicant can reduce the traffic and safety
                             concerns related to complying with this ordinance at most of the intersections by
                             continuing to work on the road profile grades to get them closer into compliance.
                             However, there is one especially problematic section of Eaglehead Way (Cordero
                             Drive) which poses an additional hazard to motorists that we don’t believe can be
                             overcome in this way. That section encompasses the Madison Peak Way/opposite
                             private alley intersection(s), the 4100 South intersection, and the area in between
                             them. In this area, the intersection grades are not met and adequate stopping sight
                                                                         Page 2 of 2
distance does not appear to be provided or achievable. It has been suggested that
one possible solution to these hazard(s) is to dead end both Madison Peak Way
and the opposite private alley prior to their connections to Eaglehead Way
(Cordero Drive) thus eliminating the intersection(s) and hazard(s). The elimination
of this intersection will resolve the grade and stopping sight distance issue at this
location and we believe the remaining intersections can be modified in such a way
as to still be safe and come closer to complying with the ordinance without
requiring a modification to the overall subdivision layout.

Jefferson Thomson, PE
